correctness.rationale: For a finite p-group, [G,G] lies in Phi(G), so every conjugacy class has one fixed image in G/Phi(G). Burnside's basis theorem reduces generation of a pair to spanning the rank-two Frattini quotient. Therefore invariable generation of two conjugacy classes is equivalent to linear independence of their quotient images. Zero images are exactly the isolated vertices; nonzero images split into p+1 projective-line parts, with all cross-part and no within-part edges. The clique, chromatic, diameter, and part-size consequences follow directly. The packaged replay checks the actual class-pair relation for four finite groups.

value.rationale: The invariably generating graph is an established graph-on-groups invariant, and the 2021 literature explicitly contrasts its connectivity with ordinary generation while pointing to clique and chromatic questions. The theorem gives an exact infinite-family structure rather than a numerical example: for every noncyclic two-generated p-group the entire reduced conjugacy-class graph is complete multipartite, with universal clique and chromatic number p+1 and diameter 2. It also identifies precisely which classes are isolated and exposes the projective-line geometry controlling adjacency.
